passages.text: MAGNET, or LOADSTONE, a ferruginous stone, which attracts iron, and, when freely suspended, turns one of its ends towards the north.
Every magnet has two poles; the like poles of two magnets repel, and the unlike attract each other.
A piece of steel rubbed upon a magnet acquires the same virtues, and keeps them; whereas soft iron loses them as soon as it is removed.
The needle does not point exactly to the north; its variation from the meridian differs in different places, and changes from year to year, at London being now about 24 degrees west.
Dr Gilbert supposed the earth itself to be a great magnet, which opinion is confirmed by the direction of the needle.
The cause of magnetism is supposed by many to be a subtle fluid which circulates through the magnet, entering at one pole and going out at the other.
A magnet is a material or object that produces a magnetic field. Lodestones, a naturally magnetized form of the iron mineral magnetite, were the first magnets known.
Every magnet has a north and a south pole. Opposite poles attract and like poles repel.
Hard magnetic materials such as some steels stay magnetized after being magnetized; soft iron loses most of its magnetism when the outside field is removed.
The Earth behaves like a large magnet, as William Gilbert proposed in 1600, which is why a compass needle points roughly north.
The Earth's magnetic poles slowly wander, so the angle between magnetic north and true north varies from place to place and changes over the years.

Magnetism arises from moving electric charges and from the spin of electrons. In 1820 Hans Christian Oersted found that an electric current deflects a compass needle, linking electricity and magnetism.

reasons: Rare terms appear in both: loadstone or lodestone, poles, steel, Gilbert.
Magnetic declination scores well but covers only the variation of the needle.
